title: Holographic heat engines for Schwarzschild black holes
abstract: We construct reversible black hole heat engines in asymptotically flat spacetime using quasi-local gravitational thermodynamics. We enclose a Schwarzschild black hole in a finite spherical cavity and identify the working substance with the dual thermal system on the cavity boundary. The surface pressure and boundary area define a thermodynamic pressure-volume pair in the dual system, while all coupling constants of the gravitational theory remain fixed. We derive exact efficiencies for the Carnot, Otto, Diesel, Brayton, and Stirling engines and compare them numerically. These efficiencies probe the quasi-local equations of state of the black hole. The regenerated Stirling efficiency remains remarkably close to the Carnot bound and approaches it in the high-temperature limit.
summary: This work develops a model for reversible heat engines powered by Schwarzschild black holes using quasi-local gravitational thermodynamics. By treating the boundary as a thermal system, the authors calculate efficiencies for various cycles, demonstrating that the regenerated Stirling efficiency approaches the Carnot limit from below at high temperatures. This provides a novel diagnostic tool linking general relativity to classical thermodynamic limits.
main_problem: The paper constructs and analyzes reversible heat engines operating using a holographic model derived from Schwarzschild black holes.
main_result: It derives efficiencies for standard heat engines (Carnot, Otto, etc.) showing that the regenerated Stirling efficiency approaches the Carnot bound from below in the high-temperature limit.
method: The analysis uses quasi-local gravitational thermodynamics applied to a black hole enclosed in a cavity, treating the boundary as the working substance.
model_or_system: The system models a Schwarzschild black hole contained within a finite spherical cavity. The thermodynamic properties of the dual thermal system on the cavity boundary are used to define the heat engine cycles.
key_observables: Efficiencies ($\eta$) for Carnot, Otto, Diesel, Brayton, and Stirling engines; quasi-local equations of state ($E(S, V)$); regenerated Stirling efficiency ($\eta_{	ext{reg}}^{	ext{Stirling}}$).
important_parameters: Temperature ratio ($T_c/T_h$); large black hole branch restriction ($0 < x < 1$); high-temperature limit ($T_h 	o \infty$).
main_assumptions: The analysis is restricted to the stable, large black hole branch; heat rejection is modeled as controlled quasi-static extraction via Hawking radiation.
paper_structure: The paper systematically derives thermodynamic relations for various strokes (isochoric, adiabatic, isobaric, isothermal) before applying these concepts to calculate the efficiencies of standard idealized heat engines and analyzing the high-temperature limits.
why_interesting: While focused on gravity, the rigorous application of classical thermodynamics principles (Carnot/Stirling cycles) to a non-standard working substance provides an advanced theoretical framework for understanding energy conversion in extreme physical systems.
